title: NovaWing Career Eval v1
purpose: A small real-repository replay set for measuring time-to-accepted-result (TTAR), first-pass acceptance, human intervention, and cost. It is engineering evidence, not a general model leaderboard.

metricDefinitions.time_to_accepted_result: Wall-clock from task submission to a reviewed ACCEPT. Infrastructure delay and required revision cycles count when externally captured.
metricDefinitions.first_pass_acceptance: Whether the first submitted implementation passed code review without a corrective implementation round.
metricDefinitions.human_intervention: Technical steering supplied by the human during execution. Ordinary permission confirmations are recorded separately when present.
metricDefinitions.cost_per_accepted_task: Observed provider cost for the accepted task when reliable billing evidence exists.

controls: Each fresh run starts from the task baseline commit.
The prompt forbids reading Git history, other branches, remote commits, PRs, or historical implementations.
The hidden reference commit is used only during review.
Harness-native orchestration is allowed; external coding agents are not.
A passing test suite alone is insufficient when required safety invariants are missing.
limitations: The pilot has a very small sample size and is not statistically generalizable.
Some early runs did not have reliable external wall-clock capture and therefore keep duration null.
Client/model display names are preserved as observed; provider routing evidence is recorded separately when needed.
A Medium Codex run is marked non-comparable because the prompt referenced a validation script absent from that baseline.

tasks.name: TypeScript exactOptionalPropertyTypes regression
acceptance: Fix the WorkSession control UI TypeScript error without behavior change.

tasks.name: Execution Ledger restart durability
acceptance: Preserve v1 phase cumulative elapsed semantics during migration.
Durable FAILED-notification success must survive a missing Ledger success fact.
Attempted-only legacy state remains eligible for one bounded retry.
Recorded delivery failure must not cause unbounded restart retries.

tasks.name: Host-owned implementation checkpoint
acceptance: Only a Host/Runtime-created and verified implementation commit may become Controller authority.
Authority binds session, task, attempt when present, dispatch/action, before observation, and after observation.
The commit proves exact parent, branch, repository identity, clean worktree, expected tree/content, scope, and link/path safety.
Checkpoint acknowledgement and durable state adoption happen before verifier/reviewer work.
Old verification/completion evidence is invalidated after adoption.
Authority is one-time and cannot be recreated from SHA, copied objects, persisted JSON, or an unowned descendant.

notes: One-file, one-line change matched the hidden historical reference exactly.
The implementation matched the hidden reference exactly.
Client wall-clock included repeated reconnect delay.
Core implementation and four required restart/migration scenarios passed review.
The prompt referenced a validation script absent from the baseline; Codex created a narrow replacement, so this run is excluded from strict timing comparison.
The DeepSeek route was externally evidenced by CC Switch and a DeepSeek account balance delta from CNY 23.12 to 22.81.
Claude Code's own final self-report incorrectly named an Anthropic model; routing evidence is treated as authoritative for this run.

notes: Only fresh H1 pilot run to reach first-pass ACCEPT.

reviewFindings: Ownership adoption happened after verifier work.
The commit tree was not bound to a pre-commit expected tree.
Hardlink safety was reported but not implemented or tested.

engineeringConclusion: The pilot supports routing by accepted-result latency rather than by model benchmark or first-response speed.
On low/medium tasks, faster DeepSeek-based harnesses reached correct results quickly with no human steering.
On the H1 security/state-consistency task, Codex High was slower than the fastest first result but was the only fresh run to reach first-pass ACCEPT.

Using the same DeepSeek route in Claude Code improved H1 first-result latency versus DeepSeek Harness High, but did not remove the same class of deep correctness misses; this suggests the harness strongly affects speed while model capability still matters for difficult invariants.
These are pilot observations from a tiny sample and should drive routing experiments, not universal model claims.
